h1: Hot-water flow changes after plumbing work
title: Hot-water flow changes after plumbing work | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand hot-water flow changes after plumbing work. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: A symptom beginning after supply isolation or plumbing work needs that history included; it should not trigger random electrical or air-gap resets.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: Tell the engineer which work was done, whether the cold supply is normal and whether all hot outlets are affected. Supply restrictions, changed components or installation conditions can require assessment of the water path.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Do not run an immersion if the cylinder may not be full. Do not dismantle strainers, turn unfamiliar safety valves or copy a draining procedure from another model.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Why is recent plumbing work relevant to a new no-flow fault?
faqs.answer: It can change the supply or water path; the work history helps direct assessment instead of assuming a heating-element failure.
